'''Paul J. Gemperline''' (born 1955) is an American [[analytical chemistry|analytical chemist]] and [[Chemometrics|chemometrician]]. He is a Distinguished Professor of Chemistry at [[East Carolina University]] (ECU) located in [[Greenville, North Carolina]] and has been the recipient of several scientific awards, including the 2003 [[Eastern Analytical Symposium]] Award in Chemometrics. He is author of more than 60 publications in the field of chemometrics.<ref name=":0" /> Dr. Gemperline served as Dean of the Graduate School at [[East Carolina University|ECU]] from 2008 to 2022.<ref name=":0" /> He retired from ECU June 30, 2022 and is now professor emeritus.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=May 2, 2022 |title=Gemperline retires as dean of ECU Graduate School |work=The Daily Reflector |url=https://www.reflector.com/news/business/gemperline-retires-as-dean-of-ecu-graduate-school/article_b36aa5db-4a70-5804-9e3f-352c6a36da75.html |access-date=March 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502092110/https://www.reflector.com/news/business/gemperline-retires-as-dean-of-ecu-graduate-school/article_b36aa5db-4a70-5804-9e3f-352c6a36da75.html |archive-date=May 2, 2022}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=ECU News Services |date=June 16, 2022 |title=Longtime ECU leaders announce retirements |work=ECU Magazine |publisher=East Carolina University |url=https://east.ecu.edu/2022/06/16/longtime-ecu-leaders-announce-retirements/ |access-date=March 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321195551/https://east.ecu.edu/2022/06/16/longtime-ecu-leaders-announce-retirements/ |archive-date=March 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name=":4" />

==Education==

Gemperline completed both undergraduate and graduate studies at [[Cleveland State University]] (CSU), graduating with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Chemistry in 1978 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Analytical Chemistry in 1982.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Paul Gemperline |url=https://chemistry.ecu.edu/faculty-staff/gemperlinep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230324144026/https://chemistry.ecu.edu/faculty-staff/gemperlinep/ |archive-date=March 24, 2023 |access-date=March 24, 2023 |website=Department of Chemistry, East Carolina University}}</ref> His dissertation was titled, "The Design of the Laboratory Network DISNET."

In 2014 CSU recognized Gemperline as a distinguished alumnus.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" /><ref name=":11" />

== Academic positions ==
Gemperline joined the chemistry faculty at East Carolina University (ECU) as an assistant professor in 1982.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> He was promoted to full professor in 1993.<ref name=":0" /> According to [[The Daily Reflector|''The'' ''Daily Reflector'']] he had a long and distinguished teaching and research career at ECU with "more than 30 years of research experience in chemometrics involving 38 undergraduate students, 20 master's students, nine visiting doctoral students and six post-doctoral research assistants" and  "more than 60 publications in the field and more than $1.8 million in external grant funds."<ref name=":0" /> He also is one of three inventors listed on a licensed patent for designing optical filters for chemical calibration.<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{cite patent |country=US |number=7138156 |inventor=Michael L. Myrick, Olusola 0. Soyemi, Paul J. Gemperline
|status= patent|title= Filter Design Algorithm for Multi-variate Optical Computing |gdate= November 21, 2006|fdate= September 26, 2001|url=https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/7138156}}</ref> He received the Helms Award for Outstanding Research from the East Carolina University Chapter of [[Sigma Xi]] in 1987, the East Carolina University Distinguished Research Professor of Chemistry (award for 5-year achievement and permanent title) in 1999, and in 2001 was made an East Carolina University College of Arts and Sciences Distinguished Professor of Chemistry,<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> an award for lifetime achievement and permanent title, given in recognition of "outstanding teaching and advising, research and creative productivity, and professional service."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Harriot College Distinguished Professorship |url=https://thcas.ecu.edu/facultyawards/ |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=East Carolina University Thomas Harriot College of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>

In 2003 Gemperline joined the university administration as associate vice chancellor of research and graduate studies.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rickert |first=Erin |date=November 2, 2003 |title=Shelton announces reorganization |work=The East Carolinian |url=https://www.piratemedia1.com/theeastcarolinian/article_0a1a71c5-7874-5313-89db-3ff61a12e36c.html}}</ref> He became dean of the Graduate School in 2008 and remained in that position until his retirement in 2022.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> Gemperline served in the positions of president-elect (2009-2010), president (2010-2011), and immediate past president (2011-2012) of the North Carolina Council of Graduate Schools.<ref>{{Cite web |title=North Carolina Council of Graduate Schools: Membership |url=https://ncgradschools.org/members/officers.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327003837/https://ncgradschools.org/members/officers.html |archive-date=March 27, 2023 |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=North Carolina Council of Graduate Schools}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
Gemperline came to the notice of a larger scientific community in 1984 with the publication of a paper describing DISNET in the ''Journal of Automated Methods and Management in Chemistry''.<ref name=PMC2547553>{{cite journal| pmc=2547553 | pmid=18927932 | doi=10.1155/S1463924684000067 | volume=6 | issue=1 | title=DISNET: a Distributed Instrument System NETwork | year=1984 | journal= Journal of Automatic Chemistry| pages=27–32 | last1 = Gemperline | first1 = PJ | last2 = Megargle | first2 = R | last3 = Dartt | first3 = A | last4 = Slivon | first4 = L | last5 = Zadnik | first5 = V| doi-access=free }}</ref> (The journal title was changed to ''Journal of Analytical Methods in Chemistry'' in 2013.) Gemperline and his colleagues provided methodologies which underlay the improvements in calibration accuracy, computer-based data acquisition and mathematical analysis in chemometrics. The qualitative advances helped open new scientific fields such as molecular modeling and [[Quantitative structure–activity relationship|QSAR]], [[cheminformatics]], the '-omics' fields of [[genomics]], [[proteomics]], [[metabonomics]] and [[metabolomics]], process modeling and [[process analytical technology]].

Gemperline is a self-taught chemometrician,<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":12">{{Cite journal |last=Haaland |first=David |date=July 2020 |title=Honoring Paul Gemperline for his 11-year service as editor-in-chief of the Journal of Chemometrics |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cem.3072 |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |language=en |volume=34 |issue=7 |article-number=e3072 |doi=10.1002/cem.3072 |s2cid=126128652 |issn=0886-9383|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and he has been most influential by dispersing knowledge of his chemometric methodologies through his publications. Perhaps the best example of this is his book, ''Practical Guide to Chemometrics'', for which he served as both editor and as a contributor.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Cutler |first=Patrick |date=March 13, 2019 |title=Paul Gemperline's contributions to chemometrics and beyond |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |volume=34 |issue=7 |article-number=e3123|doi=10.1002/cem.3123 |s2cid=126599557 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Better process methods can create inflection points that became the foundation for radical improvements and transitions in the scientific enterprise. It can be decades before the implications of particular advances are intuited, especially those related to the basic training of the next generations of chemists. His research in chemometrics has been "focused on development of new algorithms and software tools for analysis of multivariate spectroscopic measurements using pattern recognition methods, artificial neural networks, multivariate statistical methods, multivariate calibration, and non-linear model estimation."<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |date=January 12, 2007 |title=Biographies of the Guest Editors |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10408340600969437?src=recsys&journalCode=batc20 |journal=Critical Reviews in Analytical Chemistry |publisher=Taylor & Francis Group |volume=36 |issue=3–4 |page=139|doi=10.1080/10408340600969437 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Sandia National Laboratories]] researcher, David Haaland, called Gemperline a "chemometrician extraordinaire," with a "deep understanding of chemometrics" and "wide-ranging" contributions to the research literature, and said after his first meeting with Gemperline he "always read his publications and attended his talks at conferences knowing that I would learn something new every time."<ref name=":12" />

According to former graduate student, Patrick Cutler, another important aspect of Gemperline's research and teaching career has been his ability to collaborate with industry, which allowed "opportunities for students to gain invaluable experience."<ref name=":3" /> Cutler mentions pharmaceutical company [[Burroughs Wellcome]] in particular which at one time operated a production plant in Greenville, North Carolina, in close proximity to East Carolina University.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hayes |first=Thomas C. |date=April 26, 1987 |title=TRIANGLE PARK: NORTH CAROLINA'S HIGH-TECH PAYOFF |page= 12, Section 3 |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/04/26/business/triangle-park-north-carolina-s-high-tech-payoff.html |access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Gemperline collaborated with Burroughs Wellcome in the 1980s to develop software for multivariate pattern recognition analysis of near-infrared reflectance spectra for rapid, non-destructive testing of pharmaceutical ingredients and products. His research and publications in this area furthered his international recognition.<ref name=":7" /> Cutler notes that Gemperline, "built his career and has produced world-renowned chemometrics research with the limited resources of mostly undergraduates and master's level students."<ref name=":3" />

Gemperline also has had research collaborations with [[Pfizer|Pfizer, Inc]]. and [[GSK plc|GlaxoSmithKline]] and he has received "significant" funding for his research from the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) and the Measurement and Control Engineering Center (MCEC) at [[University of Tennessee|University of Tennessee, Knoxville]], an NSF-sponsored Industry-University Cooperative Research Center (IUCRC).<ref name=":7" /> He collaborated with David Haaland at Sandia National Laboratories to develop chemometric tools to study kinetics in cells using hyperspectral fluorescence imaging. Their efforts were judged successful, and led to the 2010 Meggers Award for them and coauthors Patrick Cutler and Erik Andres for their two 2009 publications in [[Applied Spectroscopy (journal)|''Applied Spectroscopy'']] about their research.<ref name=":12" /><ref>{{Cite journal |date=September 28, 2018 |title=Society Awards and Awardees Ian R. Lewis and Bonnie Saylor |journal=Applied Spectroscopy |language=en |volume=72 |issue=1_suppl |pages=16–21 |doi=10.1177/0003702818791929 |issn=0003-7028|doi-access=free |bibcode=2018ApSpe..72...16. }}</ref>

Gemperline served as the editor-in-chief of ''[[Journal of Chemometrics]]'' for ten years, from 2007 to 2017,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Trevorrow |first=Paul |date=June 8, 2020 |title=Celebrating the editorship of Professor Paul Gemperline |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc. |volume=34 |issue=7 |doi=10.1002/cem.3272 |s2cid=221546378 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gemperline |first=Paul J. |date=January 2007 |title=Editorial |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |language=en |volume=21 |issue=1–2 |page=1 |doi=10.1002/cem.1070|doi-access=free }}</ref> and before that as the North American editor for five years, from 1996 to 2001.<ref name=":5" />  The journal honored him with a special issue in July 2020.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=July 2020 |title=Special Issue: Dedicated to the editorship of Prof. Paul Gemperline |url=https://analyticalsciencejournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/toc/1099128x/2020/34/7 |journal=Journal of Chemometrics |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc. |volume=34 |issue=7}}</ref> He joined the editorial advisory board of [[Spectroscopy (magazine)|''Spectroscopy Magazine'']] in 2020.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2020 |title=Seven New Members Join Spectroscopy's Editorial Advisory Board |url=https://www.spectroscopyonline.com/view/seven-new-members-join-spectroscopy-s-editorial-advisory-board |access-date=March 20, 2023 |website=Spectroscopy Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Outside of his scientific, teaching and administrative pursuits, Gemperline enjoys cycling, sailing, kayaking, photography<ref name=":3" /> and watching [[Dancing with the Stars (American TV series)|''Dancing with the Stars'']] on [[Television|TV]].<ref name=":12" />

==Publications==

Gemperline is author of more than 60 peer-reviewed publications in the field of Chemometrics.<ref name=":0" />

His most-cited publication is his book, ''Practical Guide to Chemometrics'' ([[CRC Press]]), for which he served as both editor and as a contributor. The chapters he contributed were based on the teaching notes he had developed at East Carolina University for use with undergraduate and master's degree level students.<ref name=":3" />
